title: ACT required documents for selling a home
description: What your conveyancer needs to attach to the draft contract before the property is first offered for sale under the Civil Law (Sale of Residential Property) Act 2003. Summarised from the Access Canberra Reality Check guide.

sources.title: Reality Check: a real estate guide for buyers and sellers in the ACT

items.title: Engage a conveyancer or lawyer to prepare the draft contract
Crown lease and certificate of title
Building and lease conveyancing inquiries
items.detail: Your conveyancer orders these; they show approvals on file for the block.

items.title: Energy efficiency rating (EER) statement from an accredited assessor
Building and compliance inspection report
items.detail: Buyers can usually rely on it for 180 days, so time it close to listing.

items.title: Asbestos assessment report, or asbestos advice if there is no report
For a unit, the unit title certificate from the owners corporation
For a multi-storey unit, 2 years of owners corporation and executive committee minutes
For a pool or spa, the Pool Owners Guidance Material and a disclosure statement or compliance certificate
Check smoke alarms work (hard-wired for houses built after 1 November 1994)
Have your power of attorney, probate or other authority to sell ready
Confirm the draft contract and documents are ready before the first ad or open home
